q: In a pure metal, atoms are packed regularly in ____.
e: This regular arrangement allows layers to slide, making pure metals soft.

q: When a pure metal is alloyed, atoms of the added element have different sizes from those of the pure ____.
e: Size mismatch impedes dislocation movement, increasing hardness.
An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more elements, at least one being a metal.

q: Mixing molten tin and copper gives a gold-coloured alloy called ____.
e: Bronze is a historically significant copper-tin alloy.

q: Steel is an alloy of iron containing carbon and other ____.
e: Addition of elements like chromium or nickel tailors steel properties.

q: Traces of sulphur, phosphorus and silicon are added as modifiers of ____.
e: These elements fine-tune the mechanical and processing characteristics of steel.

q: Brass is an alloy of Cu(70%) and Zn(30%) and does not corrode ____.
e: This corrosion resistance makes brass suitable for marine applications.

q: Duralumin is an alloy of Al(93%), Cu(3%), Mg(3%) and Mn(1%) and is light and ____.
e: Its high strength-to-weight ratio is ideal for aerospace structures.

q: Stainless steel contains Fe(73%), Cr(18%), Ni(8%) and C(1%) and is hard and ____.
e: Chromium forms a passive oxide layer that prevents rusting.
